To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
HIV serodiscordant men and women can have children using assisted reproductive technology (ART), and that ART is a safe and effective method of achieving pregnancy in HIV-seropositives.
HIV-seropositivity in a man does not necessarily mean infertility.

(i) the HIV-1 viral load of semen decreases significantly after sperm washing; (ii) the risk of HIV-1 transmission by sperm washing is extremely small and comparable to the risk of transmission from an HIV-serodiscodant pregnancy; (iii) HIV-seropositivity in the mother is not associated with an increased risk of HIV-2 transmission to the infant; and (iv) HIV-2 is not transmitted by sperm washing.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of sperm washing procedures that are effective in removing HIV from semen.
the development of a sperm washing technique that will allow HIV-seroposive men to safely father a child.
the development and evaluation of sperm washing techniques for the treatment of HIV-seropositve men and their serodiscordant partners.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the risk of vertical transmission is low, and that HIV-serodiscording couples can be treated with ART.

HIV-seropositivity should not be considered a barrier to conception and that sperm washing techniques can be used to reduce or remove infectious elements from semen, allowing for successful conception in HIV-serodiscodant couples.
HIV-seropositivity is not a contraindication to assisted reproduction.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
sperm washing is safe and effective in reducing the risk of transmission to the HIV-negative partner.
the HIV-seropositivity does not affect sperm function.
the use of sperm washing techniques in HIV-serodiscordinate couples is a safe and effective method of establishing pregnancy.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the risk of HIV transmission to an uninfected partner through sperm washing is low and can be further reduced by the use of HAART.
sperm washing techniques can address the fertility needs and desires of HIV-seropostive men.
the HIV-seropositivity of a man should not preclude him and his partner from having children.
